text:
anya: Quick check-in — follow-up to the routing policy RFC. I sketched a small proposal for a precedence matrix that balances latency SLAs, regional affinity, and cost caps. PTAL: <https://go/repo/rfc-routing-observability>

olivia: skimmed — looks promising. main q: how do we measure 'regional affinity' score without blowing up the matching cost?

sam: we should avoid full graph eval on every request. idea: two-pass approach — cheap heuristics to filter candidates, exact scorer only on top-k. keeps p99 impact small.

marco: +1. cheap heuristics = bundle of three fast checks: region match, tenant-tier eligibility, and soft-cost-threshold. only then run the more expensive latency/capacity model.

anya: exactly. here's a tiny pseudo-policy example I put in the doc:

```
# precedence matrix (high -> low)
- rule: region_strict
  match: request.region == backend.region
  action: shortlist
- rule: tier_preference
  match: tenant.tier in [premium, business]
  score: +20
- rule: cost_cap
  match: backend.estimated_cost <= request.max_cost
  score: +10
- rule: fallback_any
  action: include_with_penalty
```

jin: two concerns: 1) telemetry churn if we log all intermediate matches, 2) explainer surface for support. We need sampling and aggregated counters, not verbose per-request events.

olivia: agree on sampling. For explainability: add an explain_id that can be requested only via debug endpoints, plus a per-tenant quota for traces.

sam: operational note — the shortlist size should be tunable per-region. some regions have few backends so top-k=3 might be overkill; allow dynamic k via realtime signal.

marco: can we encode the shortlist heuristic in WASM so runtime teams can hot-swap without deploys? keeps policy changes fast and bounded.

anya: interesting — wasm for filter step only. runtime work: ensure we bound cpu and latency of wasm checks (timebox to ~250us). ops-bot: deploy-check OK for wasm sandboxing?

ops-bot: CI run: wasm-sandboxer tests passed on staging. Resource limits enforced.

jin: still want to ensure we attach a cost estimate to the explain output, so support can tell customers expected token-cost delta if they force strict region. minimal fields only.

olivia: also, consider a 'grace' policy for preemptible nodes: prefer cheaper preemptible backends when latency slack > 200ms. that buys cost-savings without violating p99.

anya: summary: (1) two-pass eval: wasm cheap-filters -> exact scorer top-k (2) precedence matrix as DSL in doc (3) sampled telemetry + explain_id for debug (4) dynamic top-k per-region + grace-for-preemptible. I'll update RFC with tasks for runtime and telemetry. anyone want to own the runtime change?

sam: I can take the shortlist wasm filter integration and perf tests.

marco: I'll take the dynamic-top-k signal hookup and the preemptible heuristic.

olivia: I'll write the explain_id access policy + support docs.

anya: great — I'll add the telemetry sampling plan and a rollout checklist. thanks all :thumbsup:
